@parameters: \bAh, \PN! Did you have any questions about running the farm?
\bWhat would you like to know about?
\bPlant any Berry on a patch of soft, loamy soil out in the Orchard, and it'll grow right into a tree.
\bYou can plant Berries you've found or bought - just interact with an empty patch of soil to get started.
\bBerry trees dry out a little over time, so keep them watered with a Sprayduck, Squirt Bottle, Wailmer Pail, or Sprinklotad.
\bLet a tree dry out completely and it won't yield nearly as much when it's finally ready, so don't be shy with the watering can.
\bOnce a tree's fully grown, just interact with it to pick the Berries.
\bPicking it clears the soil right back to empty, so you'll need to plant a fresh Berry there for another batch.
\bLeave a ripe tree too long without picking it, though, and it'll sometimes sprout again on its own instead of just wilting - only so many times before it's truly spent.
\bApricorns grow just like Berries do - plant one on soft soil and water it now and then.
\bThey take a fair bit longer to mature, but a tree will go on producing for a long, long time once it gets going.
\bTake a ripe Apricorn over to Kurt at his house, and he'll turn it into a Poké Ball for you.
\bEach colour makes a different kind - Red makes a Level Ball, Yellow a Moon Ball, Blue a Lure Ball, Green a Friend Ball, Pink a Love Ball, White a Fast Ball, and Black a Heavy Ball.
\bBesides Berries and Apricorns, the fields can grow proper vegetables - Carrots, Lettuce, Potatoes, Tomatoes, Onions, Pumpkins, Corn, Wheat, and Cabbage, last I checked.
\bEach one grows a bit differently - some are quick and light, others take their time but pay better for it.
\bYou plant a seed the same way you'd plant a Berry - just interact with a bare patch of soil and choose it from your Bag.
\bOnce you've got a harvest, bring it to your Grandmother and ask her about Produce Sales. She'll pay you fair for it.
\bSpread Growth Mulch on soil before planting and whatever grows there matures about a quarter faster - though it'll dry out quicker for it.
\bDamp Mulch works the other way - growth is a touch slower, but it holds moisture much longer, so you won't need to water as often.
\bGooey Mulch means a plant that's gone too long unpicked can spring back to life more times before it's finally spent.
\bStable Mulch keeps a plant ripe and ready to pick for longer before it wilts, so you've more time to come collect it.
\bA Sprayduck, Squirt Bottle, Wailmer Pail, or Sprinklotad will all do the job.
\bJust interact with a growing plant and, if it's thirsty, it'll ask if you want to water it.
\bBerries, Apricorns, and most vegetables dry out a little every hour that goes by.
\bLet one dry out completely and it won't yield nearly as much when you finally pick it.
\bLoad the Spreader with a Berry, an Apricorn, a seed, or a bag of mulch, then just walk up to bare soil to plant it instantly, no questions asked.
\bSaves you digging through your Bag every single time.
\bSwitch on the Harvester and walk up to a ripe Berry or Apricorn tree, and you'll collect the yield without it even asking first.
\bHandy once you've got more trees than you can be bothered interacting with one at a time.
\bEverything you plant goes through a few growth stages before it's ready - you'll see it change right in front of you as it grows.
\bVegetables tend to go from freshly planted, to sprouted, to fully grown quicker than most Berry trees do.
\bPick a plant while it's ripe and the soil goes right back to empty - you'll need to replant it yourself for another batch.
\bBut leave one unpicked too long past ripe, and it'll often regrow on its own instead of dying outright - just not forever, so don't let things go to waste.
\bAn Old Rod, Good Rod, or Super Rod will all let you fish - the better the rod, the better what you'll pull up.
\bAny pond, river, or stretch of open water ought to have something biting.
\bJust stand at the water's edge and give your Rod a cast.
Putting a Pokémon in a Pen
Putting a Pokémon in a Pen
\bWe keep a few pens around the ranch. Put a Pokémon like a Miltank, Slowpoke, Chansey, Mareep, Combee, or Tauros in one, and it'll settle right in.
\bDifferent Pokémon give you different things - Moomoo Milk, a Slowpoke Tail, a Chansey Egg, Wool, Honey, or a Tauros Hide.
\bCheck back on a pen now and then to collect what's piled up - it won't spoil, but it'll stop piling up once the pen's full.
\bBring what you collect to your Grandmother and ask about Livestock Sales, and she'll pay you for it.
\bLeave two compatible Pokémon at the Day Care and, given enough time, they may produce an Egg together.
\bWe've only got room for one pair to start, though that might change if we ever expand the place.
\bA few things can influence what you get - certain held items, or certain kinds of Incense, among other things.

\bI've heard tell that with a Ditto's help, even some Pokémon that don't normally get along can produce something surprising. I couldn't say which pairs, though - you'll have to discover that yourself!
\bYour Grandmother handles all our sales. Ask her about Produce Sales for anything you've grown, or Livestock Sales for anything you've collected from the ranch pens.
\bThe fast growers won't pay as much each time, but the money keeps coming in steady. The slow ones pay better, but you'll be waiting on them.
\bMost folks do a bit of both. Find what works for you.
\bAlright! Let me know if any more questions come to mind.

\bTake care out there, and good luck with the farm!
\bAlright then. Let me know if you change your mind.
